page: Microsoft Azure D32as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 128.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The server includes 262 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the single-core CPU performance in the top 25% via stress-ng, while multi-core CPU performance falls in the middle 50% average tier. Memory performance is robust, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25%, although uncached read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks remain in the average tier. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets.

For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates strong image processing capabilities and strong text generation speeds for small 135M language models. However, it exhibits weak performance in the bottom 25% for prompt processing on large 70B language models, indicating a limitation for heavy AI inference tasks. The balanced resource allocation makes this instance suitable for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving.
